chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام, saying:
A man escorts caravans without the order of the ruler in a fearful place, and they stipulate for him a specified payment. Does he have the right to take it from them or not?
So he عليه السلام wrote: If he hires out himself for a known payment, he may take his due, if Allah wills.

key_terms.الْقَوَافِلَ: the caravans being accompanied or guarded
key_terms.حَقَّهُ: the compensation or due right owed to him
key_terms.شَيْءٍ مُسَمًّى: a specified and defined payment amount
key_terms.يُبَذْرِقُ: escorts and protects caravans on the road

ai.seo_question: Can a person lawfully take payment for escorting caravans in a dangerous area without official appointment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning payment for protective escort services provided to caravans in dangerous places. It establishes that when a person contracts himself for a clearly specified wage, he is entitled to receive that compensation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3653 - Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, wrote to Imam Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan bin Ali (as) asking:
"A man escorts caravans without the order of the ruler in a fearful place, and they agree with him on a specific payment. Is it permissible for him to take it from them or not?"
Imam (as) said: "If he hires himself out for a well-known payment, he may take his due, Allah (swt) willing."
